title: Softmax: Turning Attention Scores into Weights
objective: See what `F.softmax(att, dim=-1)` does in nanoGPT's manual attention path. Each row of scaled, masked scores becomes a set of positive weights that add up to 1, and the masked (-inf) entries end up at weight 0.
audience_context: The learner is on the Attention concept and is reading CausalSelfAttention.forward in nanoGPT's model.py, at the manual attention lines (65-71) where the softmax call appears.
scope_note: I left out the flash branch's internals, how dropout affects the weights, and the softmax formula itself, because there isn't room in 15 seconds. The flash path only appears as a branch label, and the video focuses on the softmax step in the manual path.

evidence.excerpt:
# flash attention make GPU go brrrrr but support is only in PyTorch >= 2.0
        self.flash = hasattr(torch.nn.functional, 'scaled_dot_product_attention')

# causal mask to ensure that attention is only applied to the left in the input sequence
            self.register_buffer("bias", torch.tril(torch.ones(config.block_size, config.block_size))
                                        .view(1, 1, config.block_size, config.block_size))

else:
            # manual implementation of attention
            att = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))
            att = att.masked_fill(self.bias[:,:,:T,:T] == 0, float('-inf'))
            att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)
            att = self.attn_dropout(att)
            y = att @ v # (B, nh, T, T) x (B, nh, T, hs) -> (B, nh, T, hs)

branches.runs: model.py:62-64: y = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=None, dropout_p=self.dropout if self.training else 0, is_causal=True)

claim_registry.text: On the branch where `self.flash` is false, `att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)` runs on the scaled, masked score matrix along its last dimension. Each query's row of scores over keys becomes non-negative weights that add up to 1.

On the `self.flash`-false branch, entries set to `float('-inf')` by `att.masked_fill(self.bias[:,:,:T,:T] == 0, float('-inf'))` before the softmax get exactly 0 weight after it. As a result, each position only attends to itself and earlier positions.

On the `self.flash`-false branch the steps run in this order: scores `(q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))`, then `masked_fill` with -inf, then `F.softmax(att, dim=-1)`, then `self.attn_dropout(att)`, then `y = att @ v`.
When `self.flash` is true, the code has no explicit `F.softmax` line. It calls `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=None, ..., is_causal=True)` instead.

must_show: The code line `att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)` with a label saying it belongs to the `self.flash`-false (manual) branch
A small square score grid with -inf in the cells above the diagonal (future positions)
One row being changed by softmax: raw scores, including -inf, become bars of weights
A readout showing that the row's weights add up to 1
The rest of the rows being normalized one row at a time (along dim=-1), not as one whole matrix
must_not_claim: That `F.softmax` always runs on every forward pass, whatever the value of `self.flash`
That softmax runs before the -inf mask, or that masking is applied after softmax
That dropout or `att @ v` happens before softmax
That softmax normalizes down columns (across queries) or over the whole matrix instead of along each row (dim=-1)
That softmax just picks the largest score (argmax) and sets all other entries to zero
That masked positions get a small but nonzero weight
That softmax itself produces the output `y`
That softmax changes the shape of `att`
visual_direction: Open briefly on the manual-branch code with the softmax line highlighted, then move attention to a small causal score grid. Pick out one row and show the change step by step: its raw scores, with the -inf future cells clearly marked, turn into weight bars. The -inf cells fade to zero, the remaining bars resize so they total 1, and a sum readout settles on 1. Then sweep the same change across the other rows to make clear that the normalization happens row by row. End on the resulting lower-triangular weight grid, with a small note that this matrix goes on to dropout and then `att @ v`.
